old: Its ancestor described putting things into proper rank or order, not just covering the body.
The word once lived only as a verb — to equip or array someone.
Its French root, tire, is a cousin of German Zier, meaning ornament.
clues: This noun for clothing comes from an old French verb meaning "to equip," built on a word for rank or order.
A formal, slightly dressy word for what someone is wearing, more polished than plain "clothes" or "outfit." It began as a verb for arranging and became the result itself.
Invitations may request "formal ___" and offices expect "business ___." Its old root is akin to German Zier, "ornament," and Old Norse words for glory.
